messages.author: 6a3b777d6a18967b
messages.subject: Shiny apps with choroplethr package
parts:
Hello,

I'm a big fan of shiny apps.  The dialect map that was covered in business week last year was a lot of fun to play with.

I just released a package for facilitating choropleth maps in R called choroplethr (https://github.com/trulia/choroplethr).  One of the early users of my package tried to create a shiny app using choroplethr.  In theory this would be great because then you would have an interactive map of arbitrary census data on a webpage.  He claims that he can run it locally, but that when he uploads it to rstudio's hosting service it does not work.  His issue report is here: https://github.com/trulia/choroplethr/issues/1.

I am not sure why this would be the case, but there seem to be 2 possible culprits.

1.  He claims that glimmer (is that the name of RStudio's shiny hosting service?) is using R 2.15.  Is this correct?  There seem to be some known issues with choroplethr and R 2.15.  I am about to put an explicit R version requirement because of this.  But I am not sure why glimmer would be using an old version of R.  See https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/choroplethr/Owv7NgAacGE for a discussion of the issues with version 2.15 and choroplethr.

2.  Using the census features of choroplethr requires setting an census api key with the acs.R package's api.key.install function.  I don't know how the transfer of code and state work in the upload process from a local machine to rstudio's hosting service.  Is there an init() function somewhere where the api key can be set?  Is this code publicly available (i.e. can anyone see his api key?).  

My user's shiny app is here: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/pssguy/acs/

Is there any way that I can help debug it remotely?

Thanks.

Ari

messages.author: e718c48d06f126f8
messages.subject: Re: Shiny apps with choroplethr package
parts: A short while back I had a problem with an app on the server and was told that updating R on the server would potentially break some apps and for this reason it's not done right away. My problem was with rJava so if your package uses it, that could be the problem. Just an idea.

messages.author: 4f04313c0a6b0f2f
messages.subject: Re: Shiny apps with choroplethr package
parts:
Some information on this. I took choroplethr for a test drive on the shinyapps.io site to see if that worked. The toy example that comes with the package works. http://patilv.shinyapps.io/choroplethrtestdrive/
I had to make an explicit call in server.r for the maps package. Even though it worked without that call locally, it popped an error on shinyapps.io. With the library(maps) call, the deployment was fine.

ui.r
------------
library(shiny)
shinyUI(fluidPage(
  plotOutput("pleth")
  ))

server.r
----------
library(shiny)
library(choroplethr)
library(maps)

data(county.fips, package="maps")
df = data.frame(region=county.fips$fips, value=sample(100, nrow(county.fips), replace=TRUE))
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
   
output$pleth=renderPlot({pleth=choroplethr(df, "county", 2)                                   
                                 print(pleth)})
  
})
--------------------------------

messages.subject: Re: Shiny apps with choroplethr package
parts:
Vivek and Are,

Thank you so much for your help.  I will report all of this back to my user.

The requirement for library(maps) is interesting.  I am in the process of submitting my package to CRAN, and one of the things they came back with is that in my DESCRIPTION file some packages were miscategorized as "imports", "depends", etc.  These are the types of bugs which are undetectable to me when I develop, but seem to arise when my package interacts with other packages - basically, I think that the "library(maps)" requirement is indicative of a bug that I hope gets sorted out in the CRAN submission process.

Ari
